title: Banner
description: UTSA course data service: HTTP surface, upstream Banner API client, scraper, database pool, and WebSocket subscriptions.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Running version and commit, published as a constant-1 gauge so a metric shift can be lined up against the deploy that caused it.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the process started.

panels.title: Target
panels.description: Whether the metrics endpoint answered the last scrape. When this is down every other panel renders a flat zero, which reads identically to an idle service.

panels.title: Restarts (24h)
panels.description: Process starts in the last day. A crash loop that recovers quickly leaves every other panel looking healthy, so this is the only place it shows.

panels.title: Requests/min
panels.description: All HTTP responses served, including those short-circuited by the rate limiter or the timeout.

panels.title: 5xx rate
panels.description: Share of responses that were server errors. A bare 0 here means traffic with no 5xx, not absence of data.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile across every route.

panels.title: WebSocket connections
panels.description: Currently open connections. Falls back to 0 until the first connection is made.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Top eight routes by rate, so the two dozen near-idle ones do not bury them. The ranked totals for every route are in the panel below. Fallback traffic carries its own label: ssr for a rendered page, asset for a static file.

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: Includes 429s from the rate limiter and 408s from the timeout layer, both of which sit below the metrics middleware.

panels.title: Latency distribution
panels.description: Every request rather than a quantile. Separate bands are separate populations, typically a cache hit and a database query, which p50 and p95 average into one line that matches neither.

panels.title: p95 by route
panels.description: Per-route tail latency. The histogram carries only the path label, so method and status are not separable here.

panels.title: Top routes
panels.description: Total requests over the selected range, ranked. The timeseries answers when traffic arrived; this answers how much each route actually carries.

panels.title: Latency quantiles
panels.description: Buckets span sub-millisecond cache hits through the 60s request timeout, so neither end is a cliff.

panels.title: Requests by endpoint
panels.description: Calls out to UTSA's Banner 9 API, grouped by the endpoint classifier rather than the raw URL.

panels.title: Outcomes
panels.description: Transport-level outcome. A response that arrived but failed to deserialize counts as a success here and is tracked separately as a decode failure.

panels.title: Request duration
panels.description: Round-trip time to Banner, excluding time held by the client-side rate limiter.

panels.title: Rate limiter wait
panels.description: Time a request sat in the client-side limiter before being sent. Sustained growth here means the scraper is the bottleneck, not Banner.

panels.title: Decode failures
panels.description: Responses that arrived intact but could not be deserialized, which usually means Banner changed a payload shape. Flat 0 until the first failure.

panels.title: Job outcomes
panels.description: Success as a rate on the left; failures as raw counts over the trailing 15 minutes on the right, because at a few per day they round to zero against success. Not a partition either way: recoverable_error fires per retry attempt, the others once per job.

panels.title: Courses seen
panels.description: Volume moving through completed scrapes. Fetched and unchanged track each other almost exactly; the gap between them is the interesting part. Changed is counted separately on the right axis as a raw total over the trailing 15 minutes, because as a rate it rounds to zero.

panels.title: Queue depth and age
panels.description: Jobs due to run and not locked, alongside how far behind the oldest one is. Depth flat while age climbs means the queue is stalled, not busy.

panels.title: Job duration
panels.description: How long a scrape job attempt takes, by percentile. A retried job records once per attempt, so this is attempt latency and not time-to-completion.

panels.title: Job duration distribution
panels.description: Attempt durations across their own bucket set, which runs to ten minutes rather than stopping at the 60s HTTP timeout. Empty until a build carrying banner_scrape_job_duration_seconds is deployed.

panels.title: Connection pool
panels.description: Sampled on a timer rather than on acquisition, because an exhausted pool has no acquisitions to hook.

panels.title: Failures by kind
panels.description: pool_timeout is the one that signals contention rather than a bad query. Flat 0 until the first failure.

panels.title: Connections and subscriptions
panels.description: Both are gauges kept correct by RAII guards, so a dropped connection decrements on every exit path.

panels.title: Messages
panels.description: Outbound messages are counted after the send resolves, so a failed write is visible rather than silent.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Read from procfs. Emitted as a gauge because the value is fractional, but it is monotonic and rate() applies normally.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident set is the number that counts against the container limit; virtual size is mostly address space reservations.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: A steady climb here is the usual early signature of a leaked socket or file handle.

panels.title: Container CPU
panels.description: Cgroup CPU for the pod, which includes work the process metrics miss and is the number a limit would be enforced against. Postgres is the same pod group, not the same container.

panels.title: Container memory
panels.description: Working set against the configured limit. Working set is what the kernel weighs when deciding to OOM-kill, so headroom here is the number that matters, not resident set.
